title: Personal Developer Blog (Noob)
summary: A fast, low-maintenance personal blog focused on reading experience and minimal hosting cost.
user_stories: Visitors browse a list of posts and read articles.
Author publishes new posts via git (Markdown).
Images must be optimized automatically.

security_and_compliance.security: Protect from XSS and supply-chain risks

options.justification: Produces pre-rendered HTML, excellent performance, minimal infra and cost.
Flexible for future dynamic features; slightly more complexity.
Works but loses SEO and static performance benefits.
Overkill; requires server + DB, higher maintenance and security exposure.

questions.prompt: How should content be stored and authored?

options.justification: Versioned, simple workflow, zero infra.
Great for non-dev authors but adds cost and dependency.
Works but increases maintenance for marginal benefit.
Unnecessary complexity and cost for static content.
Zero-config builds, CDN, free tier—ideal for static blogs.
Simple and free but fewer features (no built-in serverless).
Works but requires infra setup and CI integration.
Manual, error-prone, lacks automation.

title: Banking Payments API (Secure)
summary: A backend service that handles customer payments, settlement, reconciliation and audit for a mid-sized bank.
user_stories: Customers can initiate payments and view statuses.
System must reconcile transactions and produce auditable logs.
Admin can pause/high-risk transactions.

security_and_compliance.security: Encryption at rest/in transit, HSM for keys, strong auth

questions.prompt: Choose backend language / framework for core payments engine.

options.justification: Strong typing, mature ecosystem, enterprise-grade security and observability integrations.
Excellent concurrency and performance; slightly smaller ecosystem for enterprise banking specifics.
Faster to build prototypes but less suited for strict type safety and CPU-bound reconciliation tasks.
Productive for data work but not ideal for high-throughput, strongly consistent transactional engines.

questions.prompt: Choose the primary datastore for ledger and transactions.

options.justification: Supports ACID transactions, strong consistency, mature backup & replication strategies.
Global scale and strong consistency but operationally more complex/costly.
Flexible schema but harder to guarantee multi-row transactional consistency without extra work.

options.option: Event-sourced ledger on Kafka + cold store
options.justification: Powerful pattern but risky if implemented without experienced team—must still ensure durable ordering and reconciliation.

options.option: OAuth2 + mTLS + HSM for key storage
options.justification: Defense-in-depth: strong client auth, mutual TLS and hardware-backed keys for signing.
Strong and practical; cloud KMS reduces operational burden.
Works but key rotation and protection are manual and risky for banking.
Insufficient for high-risk financial operations.

title: Real-time Collaboration Whiteboard (Scaling & Realtime)
summary: A collaborative whiteboard web app where many users can draw, add sticky notes, and see real-time updates.
user_stories: Multiple users join the same board and see others' changes in <200ms.
Boards persist to storage and can be shared.
Offline edits should sync correctly when reconnected.

scale_and_performance.traffic: Variable—many concurrent rooms with dozens of users each
scale_and_performance.latency_target: <200ms for update propagation in same region

security_and_compliance.privacy: User authentication and board access control

options.justification: Low-latency bi-directional, widely supported, good for live collaboration.
Lower server bandwidth for large media; P2P can be complex for many peers.
Works for light real-time needs but not ideal for highly interactive drawing.
Too high-latency and inefficient for interactive collaboration.

questions.prompt: How to handle collaborative conflict resolution?

options.justification: Enables offline edits and deterministic merges with eventual consistency.
Proven approach (Google Docs) but more complex to implement correctly.
Simple but leads to lost edits; poor UX.
Blocks collaboration and increases friction.

questions.prompt: Choose persistent storage for board snapshots.

options.option: Object store for snapshots + small DB for metadata (S3 + Postgres)
options.justification: Cost-effective, scalable, and separates large binary blobs from structured metadata.

options.option: Document DB storing full board state
options.justification: Simpler model but may become costly for big boards.
Fast but risky if backups/failover aren't robust.

options.option: Store everything in a message queue
options.justification: Queues are not durable long-term storage; inappropriate.

title: E‑commerce Marketplace (Consistency & Payments)
summary: A multi-vendor marketplace that supports product listings, orders, payments and seller dashboards.
key_priorities: Transactional consistency for orders and inventory
user_stories: Buyers place orders and receive confirmations immediately.
Inventory must decrement atomically to avoid oversell.
Sellers see sales reports and manage listings.

scale_and_performance.traffic: Peaks during sales (spikes of tens of thousands of concurrent users)

security_and_compliance.payments: PCI scope minimized via tokenized payments

questions.prompt: Choose an architecture for order processing.

options.option: Monolithic service with strong DB transactions
options.justification: Simpler to implement but can be hard to scale for spikes.
Enables independent scaling, decoupling and eventual consistency with compensating actions.

options.option: Serverless functions per action with shared DB
options.justification: Fast to scale for spikes but needs careful transaction design.

options.option: Heavy reliance on third-party marketplace platform
options.justification: May limit customization and vendor lock-in risk.

options.option: Single relational DB with row-level transactions
options.justification: Simple and safe for small scale; may become bottleneck at massive scale.

options.option: CQRS with read models (elastic search) and write DB (Postgres)
options.justification: Separates read/write concerns, helps scale reads during events and prevents oversells.
Fast but needs strong measures to avoid consistency issues.

options.option: No DB; rely on payment provider for stock
options.justification: Not viable—inventory must be owned by platform for accurate listings.

title: IoT Fleet Management (Edge & Intermittent Connectivity)
summary: Manage thousands of edge devices (vehicles/drones) that occasionally go offline and must report telemetry and receive OTA updates.
key_priorities: Secure OTA updates and device identity
user_stories: Devices buffer telemetry offline and sync when online.
Admin triggers OTA update with rollback support.
System detects rogue devices and quarantines them.

scale_and_performance.devices: Thousands of devices with bursty connectivity
scale_and_performance.ingestion: High write throughput during reconnect windows

security_and_compliance.data: Encrypted telemetry and secure OTA signing

options.justification: Lightweight, handles intermittent connectivity and supports QoS and retained messages.
Simple but heavier on bandwidth and less ideal for intermittent connections.
Very lightweight but less common tooling and more operational complexity.

options.option: Plain TCP sockets with custom protocol
options.justification: Reinventing the wheel; fragile and hard to secure/scale.

questions.prompt: How to implement OTA updates safely?

options.option: Signed artifacts + version pinning + staged rollout
options.justification: Ensures authenticity, allows rollback and reduces blast radius.

options.option: Push full images to all devices immediately
options.justification: Risky—no staged rollout or verification.
Efficient but insecure without signing/verification.

options.option: Require manual USB updates in safe facilities
options.justification: Secure but operationally costly and slow.

title: Healthcare Teleconsultation (HIPAA/Privacy)
summary: Video + chat teleconsultation platform for clinics requiring strict privacy, audit trails, and scheduling.
user_stories: Patients book appointments and join encrypted video calls.
Doctors access patient's history during session with strict RBAC.
Audit logs for all access and changes must be retained.

security_and_compliance.requirements: Encrypted PII, signed BAAs, retention policies

questions.prompt: Choose video architecture for secure consults.

options.option: Managed HIPAA-compliant video (e.g., Twilio with BAA)
options.justification: Reduces compliance burden, provides encryption and media relay.
More control and potential cost savings but requires compliance ops and hardening.
Lower server cost but harder to audit, record, and enforce corporate network controls.
Non-compliant and insecure for PHI.

options.option: OIDC with MFA + short-lived session tokens and device binding
options.justification: Strong identity guarantees, helps prevent session hijack.
Convenient and reasonable security but needs careful link expiry and phishing mitigation.
Basic protection but weak for sensitive healthcare flows.
Violates privacy and compliance requirements.

options.option: Prometheus + Grafana + Jaeger + ELK for logs (centralized)
options.justification: Full-stack monitoring, tracing and centralized logs; essential for audits and incident response.
Simpler to operate but limited customization and potential cost.
Works for small setups but poor for debugging and compliance reporting.
Unacceptable for production healthcare systems.

interview_style_questions: How would you design end-to-end encryption for stored consultations while enabling authorized auditing?
Explain how you'd implement role-based access (doctor, nurse, admin, patient) and emergency break-the-glass flows.

title: Short-form Video Social App (High Throughput)
summary: Mobile-first app for short videos with feeds, likes, and personalized recommendations.
user_stories: Users upload short videos, watch personalized feeds, like/comment, and share.

options.option: Object store (S3) + serverless transcode (Lambda or Cloud Functions)
options.justification: Scales cheaply, integrates with CDN and event-driven processing.

options.option: Self-hosted storage + FFmpeg workers on VMs
options.justification: More control and possibly cost-effective at massive scale but higher ops burden.

options.option: Store original on DB and transcode on upload synchronously
options.justification: Slow uploads and poor user experience.

options.option: Store media in relational DB blobs
options.justification: Very inefficient and costly for large media.

options.option: Precomputed feed per user (pipeline + Redis for fast reads)
options.justification: Low-latency reads suitable for massive view traffic.

options.option: Real-time compute on request using ranking model
options.justification: Simpler but high CPU per request; can cause latency spikes.
Easy to implement but poor personalization.

options.option: Push all feeds via email/notifications only
options.justification: Not applicable to video consumption UX.

questions.prompt: Cost-control strategy for serving video at scale.

options.option: Use CDN with tiered caching + object lifecycle + spot instances for batch work
options.justification: Reduces egress and storage costs, uses cheap compute for non-critical processing.

options.option: Always-on large VMs and dedicated storage
options.justification: Expensive and inefficient for variable workloads.

options.option: Rely on fully managed third-party hosting with high egress fees
options.justification: Simple but can be costly as scale grows.

options.option: Edge functions for transcoding on upload
options.justification: Low latency but may be limited by function runtimes and cost per execution.

interview_style_questions: Design an upload pipeline that minimizes user's perceived latency and ensures eventual consistency of feed.
How would you prevent hot objects (viral videos) from overloading origin servers during a spike?

title: ML Model Serving Platform (Batch & Online)
summary: Platform to serve ML models for low-latency online inference and periodic batch re-training & backfilling.
user_stories: Models serve personalized recommendations in <50ms.
Data science teams can deploy new models and roll back quickly.

security_and_compliance.data: PII handling and feature access control

questions.prompt: Choose serving infrastructure for online inference.

options.justification: Flexible, supports GPUs and real-time autoscaling with versioning.
Simple to operate but cold-starts and GPU access are limited.

options.option: Monolithic web app hosting models in-process
options.justification: Simple but hard to scale and risky for isolation.

options.option: Batch-only inference with cache for online
options.justification: Cannot meet low-latency online requirements reliably.

questions.prompt: Feature store choice for low-latency features.

options.option: Dedicated feature store (Feast) + low-latency serving DB
options.justification: Ensures consistent online/offline features and low latency lookups.

options.option: Materialized views in Redis from ETL jobs
options.justification: Fast but more fragile to keep in sync during re-trains.

options.option: Direct DB queries to OLTP DB
options.justification: High latency and coupling with transactional systems.
No separation of concerns or reusability.

options.option: Use GPU spot/preemptible instances for batch training and reserved for online
options.justification: Cheap for batch, reliable for latency-critical online workloads.
Costly when utilization is low.

options.option: CPU-only inference with highly optimized models
options.justification: Works for small models but may not meet latency for complex models.

options.option: Offload to third-party ML serving providers with per-request pricing
options.justification: Reduces ops but can be expensive at scale.

interview_style_questions: How would you design model rollout and canarying to detect performance regressions?
Explain strategies to keep online and offline features consistent during retraining.

title: B2B Analytics Dashboard (Security & Multi-tenant)
summary: SaaS analytics dashboard for enterprise customers with multi-tenant isolation and exportable reports.
user_stories: Admins invite tenant users and control data access.
Tenants run reports and export CSV/PDFs.

options.option: Single-tenant DB per customer (schema per tenant)
options.justification: Strong isolation and compliance; higher cost but simpler reasoning for security.

options.option: Shared DB with row-level tenant column + RBAC
options.justification: Cost-effective but needs careful access control testing.

options.option: Shared DB + separate index per tenant
options.justification: Compromise but can be fragile at scale.

options.option: Single global dataset without tenant segregation
options.justification: Non-compliant and insecure.

options.option: React + WebAssembly for heavy client-side computation
options.justification: Powerful but adds engineering complexity.
Balances interactivity with server-side performance and security.
Low interactivity and UX.
Obsolete and insecure.

options.option: Structured logs with tenant-id, metrics per-tenant and quota alerts
options.justification: Enables debugging and SLA reporting per tenant.
Insufficient for tenant investigations.
Cannot attribute issues to tenants.
Strong isolation but higher operational cost.

interview_style_questions: How would you design tenant onboarding with secure data isolation and cost tracking?
What strategies prevent a noisy neighbor tenant from impacting others' performance?

title: Small Business POS (Offline-first Cashier App)
summary: Point-of-sale system for small shops that must operate offline and sync sales later.
user_stories: Cashiers can take sales when network is down; sync when online.
Managers can reconcile daily reports.

security_and_compliance.payments: Use tokenized card readers to avoid PCI scope

options.option: Electron desktop app with local DB (SQLite)
options.justification: Cross-platform, supports local storage and offline sync.

options.option: PWA with IndexedDB and service workers
options.justification: Lightweight, easy installs, offline-capable, lower footprint.
Good UX but maintenance overhead for platforms.
Fails offline requirement.

options.option: Local append-only log with idempotent server reconciliation
options.justification: Resilient to retries and ensures no duplicates.

options.option: Sync via manual CSV upload by manager
options.justification: Workable but error-prone and slow.

options.option: One-shot full DB replace on reconnect
options.justification: Dangerous and likely to lose recent transactions.

options.option: Optimistic sync with simple last-write wins
options.justification: Simple but needs care to avoid lost transactions.

questions.prompt: How to handle card payments to reduce PCI scope?

options.option: Use PCI-compliant tokenized card readers and redirect flows
options.justification: Reduces scope and complexity for compliance.
High risk and compliance burden.

options.option: Process payments through a third-party SDK with hosted fields
options.justification: Practical compromise for many SMBs.
Simple but impractical for many customers.

interview_style_questions: Explain an idempotent reconciliation algorithm used to merge offline sales.
How would you test offline sync behavior at scale for a franchise with many stores?

title: Ad Exchange / Real-Time Bidding (Low Latency)
summary: RTB platform to bid on ad impressions with sub-100ms decision windows.
user_stories: DSPs connect and bid in real-time; publishers see revenue reports.

options.option: Highly-optimized C++/Rust bidding engines colocated in edge POPs
options.justification: Lowest latency and predictable performance.
Good balance of performance and developer productivity.
May struggle under extreme QPS with GC and single-threaded model.
Too slow for strict latency requirements.

questions.prompt: Placement of servers to meet latency goals.

options.option: Colocate in provider edge/POP near exchange endpoints
options.justification: Reduces network RTT and improves decision time.

options.option: Single central region with high-capacity links
options.justification: Higher RTT may miss bids.
Flexible but cold starts can add jitter.

options.option: Only on-premise data centers far from exchanges
options.justification: Bad for latency-critical RTB.

questions.prompt: Observability for latency spikes and dropped bids.

options.option: Real-time sampling traces + p99/p999 latency dashboards and alerting
options.justification: Necessary to detect tail latency affecting revenue.
Too slow to diagnose real-time issues.

options.option: Basic request counters and error rates
options.justification: Useful but not sufficient for tail latency analysis.

options.option: Synthetic bid traffic monitoring from edge locations
options.justification: Helps detect regional issues proactively.

interview_style_questions: How would you design a stateless bidding flow to maximize throughput?
Describe methods to ensure fairness and prevent bid shading or fraud.

title: Cryptocurrency Exchange (Security & Compliance)
summary: Order-matching and custody platform for crypto assets, with strict security and regulatory needs.
user_stories: Users deposit/withdraw funds, trade, and view balances.
Platform must maintain provable reserves and prevent double-spends.

options.option: Hardware wallets for cold storage + HSM-backed hot wallets with multisig
options.justification: Industry practice: minimizes theft risk and supports audits.

options.option: Cloud KMS alone for all keys
options.justification: Simpler but increases risk if cloud account compromised.

options.option: Store private keys encrypted in DB
options.justification: High risk and not acceptable for exchange custody.
Reduces operational burden but requires trust and costs.

options.option: In-memory matching engine with durable WAL and periodic snapshots
options.justification: High performance and crash-recovery; industry standard.

options.option: Relational DB driven matching with transactions
options.justification: Simpler but may not meet latency and throughput needs.

options.option: Event-sourced matching via Kafka and consumers
options.justification: Scalable and auditable but adds complexity.

options.option: Outsource matching to a third-party exchange
options.justification: Loss of control and potential compliance issues.

options.option: Integrate with reputable KYC providers + in-house AML analytics
options.justification: Balances speed, coverage and regulatory compliance.
Slow and costly; impractical at scale.
Regulatory risk and limited fiat on/off ramps.

options.option: Basic checks with deferred verification for small limits
options.justification: Trade-off between friction and compliance for low-value users.

interview_style_questions: Explain how you'd design proof-of-reserves and verifiable audits to reassure users.
How would you architect withdrawal rate limits and hot-wallet thresholds to limit exposure?

title: Supply Chain Tracking (Blockchain & Provenance)
summary: Track goods across multiple organizations, ensure provenance and tamper-evident records for compliance.
user_stories: Partners record handoffs; regulators can audit provenance.

options.option: Permissioned blockchain (Hyperledger) with off-chain data and on-chain hashes
options.justification: Good balance of trust and performance for consortiums.
Transparent but expensive and slow for high-volume records.

options.option: Centralized DB with cryptographic hashes stored externally
options.justification: Simpler and cheaper; weaker decentralization guarantees.
Not tamper-evident or scalable.

questions.prompt: How should partners integrate their systems?

options.option: Standardized event APIs + signed messages + webhooks
options.justification: Interoperable and auditable across organizations.
Works but brittle and hard to audit.
Security and governance nightmare.
Practical but needs maintenance.

interview_style_questions: Describe tradeoffs between storing full payload on-chain vs only hashes.
How would you handle a partner that refuses to adopt the standard API?

summary: Mobile app for microlearning with quizzes, spaced repetition, and offline access.
user_stories: Students complete lessons and quizzes offline and sync progress.
Teachers view class-level analytics.

security_and_compliance.data: Minimal PII, parental consent flows for minors

options.justification: Best UX but higher development cost.
Strong tradeoff: near-native UX with lower dev cost.
Poor performance on low-end devices.
Limited native integration and offline installability on some platforms.
Robust offline-first approach suitable for low-connectivity environments.

options.option: Cache content in service worker only
options.justification: Limited for structured progress data.
Fails requirement.
Storage limits and reliability issues.

options.option: Batch ETL to a data warehouse (BigQuery/Redshift) + BI dashboards
options.justification: Enables rich analytics and scaling.

options.option: Real-time dashboards with expensive OLAP store
options.justification: Faster insights but higher cost.
Simple but limited interactivity.
Undermines teachers' needs.

Explain accessibility considerations for low-vision users on mobile.
